algorithm_lessons.title: Kahn’s algorithm
algorithm_lessons.why: Understand the eligibility rule that every priority-based variant must preserve.
algorithm_lessons.video_match: Topological-sorting lecture; source-removal code below is separately checked
algorithm_lessons.watch_for: Why a task with zero remaining indegree can be chosen, and why a queue avoids repeatedly searching every vertex.
steps: Initialize a queue with every zero-indegree task.
Remove one task, append it to the order, and decrement each successor’s indegree.
Enqueue a successor only when its count becomes zero. Reject the graph if fewer than n tasks are output.
algorithm_lessons.formula: d_D(v) = |pred(v) ∖ D|;  choose only v with d_D(v) = 0.
algorithm_lessons.proof: The indegree invariant makes each chosen task eligible. Removing its outgoing edges preserves the invariant. A nonempty residual DAG has a source, so an empty queue before completion implies a cycle.
algorithm_lessons.cost: O(n + m) time with adjacency lists and a deque; O(n) auxiliary space beyond the graph and output.
algorithm_lessons.warning: Kahn is not ordinary BFS. BFS discovering a task does not mean all its prerequisites are satisfied. Residual blocked tasks need not all lie on a cycle.

algorithm_lessons.title: DFS ordering and cycle detection
algorithm_lessons.why: Learn an independent way to verify ordering and detect cycles.
algorithm_lessons.watch_for: The active recursion stack, finish order, and the reason to reverse that order.
steps: Mark a task active, then visit its unseen successors.
An edge to an active task is a directed-cycle witness.
Append a task only after its successors finish; reverse the complete finishing list.
algorithm_lessons.formula: For every edge u → v in a DAG, finish(v) < finish(u).
algorithm_lessons.proof: If v is unseen, DFS finishes v before returning to u. If v is finished, its finish already precedes u’s. An active v would create a cycle, so that case is excluded in a DAG.

algorithm_lessons.code:
def consumer_events(consumers: Iterable[int], completion_order: Sequence[int],
                    size: int) -> list[dict]:
    """Illustrate a single file. All initial consumers are already eligible.

    Sets make the surviving consumer visible; this is not an optimized scheduler.
    The empty-set transition is lifetime accounting, not a second credit event.
    """
    if size < 0:
        raise ValueError("Negative file size")
    remaining = set(consumers)
    if len(completion_order) != len(remaining) or set(completion_order) != remaining:
        raise ValueError("Complete each distinct consumer exactly once")
    initial = next(iter(remaining)) if len(remaining) == 1 else None
    rows = [{"finished": None, "remaining": sorted(remaining),
             "credit_to": initial, "credit": size if initial is not None else 0}]
    for u in completion_order:
        old = len(remaining)
        remaining.remove(u)
        credit_to = next(iter(remaining)) if old == 2 else None
        rows.append({"finished": u, "remaining": sorted(remaining),
                     "credit_to": credit_to, "credit": size if credit_to is not None else 0})
    return rows
